audit_findings.detail: The a002 response is structurally invalid and accepted_call is null. The selected step value is a program-isolated partial fragment retaining 633 modeled IR. Its 10 model gap records contain two unmodeled IR and eight ordinary limitations; the 44 validation-origin gaps in result.json produce 54 combined gap records. Those numbers describe different sets and must not be interchanged.

The two source-declared unmodeled IR are absent mobile and rich-results sections yielding JavaScript undefined. The supplied reasons distinguish undefined from null and explain serialization consequences. They are separate from the 44 program-isolated records.

The missing report-RPC dispatch now has a source-evidenced empty specification and is retained. The correction also represents 46 of the former 48 source-unmodeled IR. Passing record coverage does not establish their source semantics.

All 25 physical saveResult sites remain modeled as a direct write of input[0] to category-level symbolic storage. Actual saveResult creates a wrapper containing data and metadata, incorporates current settings/propertyId, time, category and labels, derives a concrete path, and serializes that wrapper. The selected summaries do not construct this wrapper or bind the dynamic path. The prose at ir_115 claims metadata wrapping while its operations still write input[0] only. The separate saveResult function body does not by itself connect those summaries to their physical call occurrences.

CFG input[2] is already [{name:pagePath},{name:pageTitle}], but the retained processing for_each builds {name:item} for each existing object, producing nested names. The source passes the object array directly; only the metric-name strings require mapping. This is a source mismatch despite retention by structural validation.

The correction introduces separate pre-request and post-request error cases for the two high-level loops; post-request cases explicitly deliver publish/inspect requests. Normal branches and the low-level batch still invoke local tool locations update/inspection, rather than explicit remote events, and omit the per-URL console event inside the protected body. Separate standalone remote IR do not establish member-specific normal-path remote coverage. The ordinary gaps accurately retain uncertainty about response acquisition before a later exception.

All 25 formerly unmodeled high-level child acquisitions are now retained as local tool calls and separate category-storage writes. This recovers modeled records and explicit default-save effects, but does not by itself model the child invocation's actual network request/response, helper defaults, save wrapper, dynamic path or receiver identity. Do not equate the higher modeled count with those external boundaries being covered.

The 13 direct calls retain remote request/response operations. Their generic locations do not bind the CFG method receiver. The model now records this explicitly at ir_110, including the unknown SDK token-exchange relation. Several interface contracts cite actual request construction and say those fields select an operation; current supplied fields alone do not establish the interface's sufficient-and-necessary field requirements. This snapshot does not establish verified minimal contracts.

The ordinary gap still records absent summary reader binding, Markdown transform and Markdown write coordinates, plus the lack of invocation-to-file binding. Task analysis-summary remains a documented obligation, not a fulfilled source boundary.

Isolation includes resource handles, client-cache writes, save defaults, response projections, clock reads, save filename/metadata clocks and load dispatch/projections. Although all direct remote and physical save-site IR survive, surrounding and upstream records do not. Only saved propagation records can later establish which concrete sites were actually processed.
